This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start

- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.

- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52

              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 说出前缀缓存的缓存键是什么：由「位置 + 块内容 + 父块哈希 + salt」构成的 lineage 哈希链，以及为什么共享前缀的请求会得到完全相同的键。

13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	本讲假设你已读过 u2-l1（BlockPool 与 padding 块）和 u2-l2（RequestKv 生命周期）。在此之上补充四个通俗概念：
16	
17	- **前缀缓存（prefix cache）**：很多请求共享同一个 prompt 前缀（系统提示词、多轮对话的历史、few-shot 示例）。这些 token 的 K/V 一旦算过一次，后到的请求就没必要再算一遍——把已算好的整块 KV 直接挂给新请求，跳过这部分 prefill。收益非常直观：Qwen3-4B 上一个 ~1900 token 的重复 prompt，首 token 延迟（TTFT）从 141.8ms 降到 16.3ms（约 8.7 倍），见 [docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md:L1-L16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md#L1-L16)。
18	- **LoRA**：一种轻量微调方案——基座模型权重不动，额外挂一组很小的「适配器」权重参与前向。同一个 prompt 在不同适配器下会算出**不同的 K/V 字节**。这是本讲 salt 机制的直接动因。
19	- **盐（salt）**：密码学借来的词——计算哈希时混入的一段额外输入。同一个内容配上不同的盐，得到完全不同的哈希。把 LoRA 名当盐混进块哈希链，就能让「同 token 不同适配器」的块永远互相不可见。
20	- **活跃池 / 非活跃池**：承接 u2-l1 的结论——请求 `release()` 之后，它注册过的完整块不回空闲池，而是进入 LRU 管理的**非活跃池**（可被前缀匹配复活，也可能被回收）；正在被请求持有或被强引用钉住的块在**活跃池**。前缀缓存命中就是从这两个池里「认领」块。

35	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
36	
37	### 4.1 块哈希链：前缀缓存的键
38	
39	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
40	
41	前缀缓存的第一个问题是：**怎么判断「这个块以前算过」？** 答案是给每个完整块算一个内容身份。但单块内容哈希不够——同一个 16-token 片段出现在序列不同位置时语义不同（RoPE 位置编码不同），也不能直接当缓存键。kvbm 的做法是 **lineage 哈希链**：每个块的哈希覆盖「它自己的内容 + 它在序列中的位置 + 父块的哈希」，概念上：
42	
43	\[
44	h_0 = H(\text{salt},\ \text{pos}_0,\ c_0), \qquad
45	h_i = H(\text{salt},\ \text{pos}_i,\ c_i,\ h_{i-1})
46	\]
47	
48	这样第 \(i\) 块的哈希实际上代表了「从序列开头到第 \(i\) 块」的完整历史——两个 prompt 只要前缀相同，前缀上每一块的哈希都逐位相同；一旦某块内容分叉，它和之后所有块的哈希全部不同。源码注释的原话是 "position + content + parent fragment, so block `i` of prompt `P` hashes the same no matter which request computed it"（见 [src/pool.rs:L635-L642](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L635-L642)）。
49	
50	第二条设计：**salt 从链头就混入**。salt 变了，整条链从 \(h_0\) 起全部改变——这就是 LoRA 隔离的全部原理。
51	
52	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
53	
54	- 请求创建时：`tokens + block_size + salt` → `TokenBlockSequence`，内部为每个**封满**的块推导 lineage 哈希。

68	/// Returns all sequence hashes from completed blocks.

76	16 字节内容键的打包在 [src/pool.rs:L735-L739](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L735-L739)：

107	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

109	**练习 1**：为什么不用「整条 prompt 的哈希」做缓存键，而要逐块建链？

117	
118	### 4.2 PrefixProbe：probe_prefix 与加盐链路
119	
120	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
121	
122	探测（probe）回答的问题是：「这个 prompt 的前缀，现在 GPU 上已经有多少块？」它**不创建请求、不预约调度**，只产出一个只读的 `PrefixProbe`。它的原始动机是 KV offload 的 CPU 层预取（u3-l1 详讲），但它的字段清晰地划分了四个容易混淆的「块数」口径：
123	
124	- `gpu_hit_blocks`：GPU 上已经命中的连续前缀块数。
125	- `held_blocks`：探针实际用强引用**钉住**的块数（GPU 命中 + 之后从 CPU 层提交进来的块）。
126	- `reusable_blocks`：真正允许被请求复用的块数 = `min(held, cacheable)`。
127	- `cpu_query_window`：还需要去 CPU 层查询的块数 = `cacheable − gpu_hit`。
128	
129	其中「可复用上限」服从本讲最重要的公式。设 prompt 长度为 \(n\)、块大小为 \(b\)：
130	
131	\[
132	\text{cacheable} = \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{b} \right\rfloor
133	\]
134	
135	即**永远比「整条 prompt 能凑出的满块数」少留出至少一个 token**。若 \(n\) 恰为 \(b\) 的整数倍，则最后**一整块**都不可复用。
136	
137	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
138	
139	```text
140	probe_prefix(prompt, lora)
141	  └─ probe_prefix_with_cache_salt(prompt, cache_salt=None, lora)
142	       ├─ new_request_with_cache_salt(prompt, 0, cache_salt, lora)
143	       │     ├─ salt_hash = compute_salt_hash(cache_salt, lora)   ← 加盐点
144	       │     └─ SchedulableSequence::new(..., Some(salt_hash))    ← 链头混入
145	       ├─ seq_hashes = 该临时请求的 all_sequence_hashes()
146	       ├─ cacheable = (n - 1) / block_size                        ← 留最后一个 token
147	       └─ gpu_guard = block_manager.match_blocks(&seq_hashes)     ← 线性前缀匹配
148	  → PrefixProbe { seq_hashes, gpu_hit, cacheable, block_size, held: gpu_guard }
149	```
150	
151	注意：公共入口 `probe_prefix` 固定 `cache_salt = None`，`cache_salt` 变体目前是 crate 私有（`fn` 而非 `pub fn`），供 MTP 等「同样 token 会因块外状态产生不同 KV」的场景在 crate 内部使用——对外公开的身份维度只有 `lora_name`。

248	### 4.3 match_and_add_prefix：挂前缀与「永远留最后一个 token」
249	
250	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
251	
252	匹配是前缀缓存的**消费**动作：在请求第一次 `schedule_prefill` 之前调用一次，把命中的整块直接挂进该请求的块指派表，返回可跳过的 token 数，`kv_position` 同步前移——之后 prefill 只需转发剩余后缀。「永远留最后一个 token」在 kvbm 上游被强制执行，理由有二（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs:L428-L441](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs#L428-L441) 的注释原文）：

254	1. **采样需要**：最后一段 prefill 必须跑，才能用最后一个位置的 logits 采样出**第一个生成 token**（全命中会导致无 forward 可做）。

356

358	- `BlockPool::active_prefix_hashes`：只查**活跃池**前缀，不晋升非活跃条目、不钉住块——一个「看一眼还活着多长前缀」的只读探照灯。
359	- 上游 LRU 非活跃索引：块释放 → 进 LRU；新分配缺块 → 从 LRU 最旧端弹出复用；前缀命中 → 从索引中弹出（复活为活跃）。

402	上游的两副面孔（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/manager/mod.rs:L87-L95](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/manager/mod.rs#L87-L95) 与 [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs:L65-L86](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs#L65-L86)）：

406	pub fn evict_inactive(&self) {
407	    drop(self.store.drain_inactive_to_mutable());
408	}
409	
410	// LRU 后端: 分配缺块时从最旧端弹出（隐性回收）
411	fn allocate(&mut self, count: usize) -> Vec<(SequenceHash, BlockId)> {
412	    for _ in 0..count {
413	        if let Some(entry) = self.cache.pop_lru() { allocated.push(entry); } ...
414	}
415	
416	fn insert(&mut self, seq_hash: SequenceHash, block_id: BlockId) {
417	    assert!(self.cache.len() < self.cache.cap().get(),
418	        "LRU backend insert would cause eviction! ...");

420	
421	这段代码做了什么：回收有两条路——**显式** `evict_inactive` 全量冲刷、**隐性** `allocate` 从 LRU 最旧端取；`insert` 的断言表明 LRU 容量按「能装下全部块」配置，正常路径绝不静默丢条目。

423	消费侧的一个真实用法（[pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L2505-L2521](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L2505-L2521)）：纯 L2 模式下，qwen3 在探测前先 `evict_inactive()` 清掉跨请求的 HBM 留存，让 `probe_prefix` 看到 `gpu_hit == 0`、整段可复用前缀都去 CPU 层查询——evict 在这里是「测量开关」而不是内存压力应对。

425	#### 4.4.4 代码实践

428	2. **操作步骤**：阅读并运行内联测试 `active_prefix_hashes_exclude_reclaimable_entries`（[src/pool.rs:L778-L789](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L778-L789)，纯逻辑无 GPU）：

430	   ```bash
431	   cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --lib active_prefix_hashes -- --nocapture
432	   ```
433	
434	   场景：40-token prompt，prefill 32 token（2 块）后——`active_prefix_hashes` 长度为 2（块仍被请求持有）；`release()` 之后——立刻变空。
435	3. **需要观察的现象**：两段断言先后通过：持有期 2、释放后 0。
436	4. **预期结果**：如上。随后思考：此时若 `match_and_add_prefix` 同 prompt 新请求，仍能命中 2 块（块在**非活跃池**里，`match_blocks` 同时查两个池）——这正是 4.3 实践里 `lora_salt_isolates_prefix_cache` 的前半段铺垫。待本地验证。

438	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
439	
440	**练习 1**：`evict_inactive` 会不会误伤正在服务的请求？padding 块会不会被清掉？
441	**答案**：都不会。它只 drain 非活跃池；在用块由请求的强引用保持在活跃池。padding 块被 `std::mem::forget` 的 RAII 把手钉死在活跃池（u2-l1），天然免疫。

443	**练习 2**：非活跃池里的块什么时候被**隐性**回收？

449	## 5. 综合实践
450	
451	把本讲三个机制（加盐哈希链、匹配挂前缀、非活跃池复活）串成一个完整剧本——这就是规格指定的核心实践：**复现 `lora_salt_isolates_prefix_cache` 的场景并补全状态追踪**。
452	
453	**任务设定**：`KvCacheManager` 以 32 块、block_size=16 建池（1 块 padding → 31 可用）。prompt 为 48 个 `7`（3 个满块）。
454	
455	**步骤**（参照 [tests/lifecycle.rs:L237-L270](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/tests/lifecycle.rs#L237-L270) 逐行跟踪，先填表再跑测试）：
456	
457	| 步骤 | 操作 | 预期 `available_blocks()` | 预期匹配结果 |
458	|---|---|---|---|
459	| 1 | 请求 a（`Some("a")`）`schedule_prefill(48)` + `apply_prefill(42)` | 31 → 28（3 块被占） | — |
460	| 2 | `a.release()` | 28 → 31（3 块进**非活跃池**，不回空闲池也计为可用） | — |
461	| 3 | 基座请求（`None`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31 | **0**：salt 不同，哈希链从第 0 块就不同 |
462	| 4 | 请求 b（`Some("b")`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31 | **0**：同上 |
463	| 5 | 请求 a2（`Some("a")`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31（2 块从非活跃池复活为活跃） | **32**：3 块全部哈希命中，但 cacheable = ⌊47/16⌋ = 2 钳掉 1 块 |
464	
465	验证命令（需 CUDA）：
466	
467	```bash
468	cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --test lifecycle lora_salt -- --nocapture
469	```
470	
471	无 GPU 时用等价的纯逻辑内联测试覆盖同一机制（cache_salt 维度）：`cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --lib cache_salt_isolates -- --nocapture`（[src/pool.rs:L791-L835](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L791-L835)，其中还能看到探测路径同样被隔离：错误 salt 的 `probe_prefix` 得 `gpu_hit_blocks() == 0`）。断言数值待本地验证。
472	
473	**最后回答规格的问题：如果去掉 salt，两个不同 LoRA 适配器会出什么正确性事故？**
474	
475	块哈希将只由 token 内容、位置与父链决定——适配器 a 注册的块与适配器 b 的请求算出**完全相同的键**。于是 b 的 `match_and_add_prefix` 会命中 a 算出的块，跳过这段 prefill，注意力内核随后拿着**用 a 的权重算出的 K/V** 去和 **b 的权重算出的 Q** 做点积。这不是崩溃，而是**静默的输出污染**：分布悄悄漂移，没有任何断言或错误会触发（源码注释的措辞正是 "K/V computed with different weights can't be **silently** reused"——salt 的作用就是让这种复用在键空间里直接不可能，而不是在挂载时检查）。反向同样成立：基座请求会误吃 LoRA 块、LoRA 请求会误吃基座块。由于同一条哈希链还被 offload 的 CPU 层查询与路由事件复用，隔离在键推导处做一次，所有层自动生效。
476	
477	## 6. 本讲小结
478	
479	- 前缀缓存的键是 **lineage 哈希链**：位置 + 块内容 + 父块哈希 + salt，共享前缀逐位相同、分叉即全变；尾部半块永不参与（只匹配整块）。
480	- **永远留最后一个 token**：cacheable = ⌊(n−1)/b⌋ 在 kvbm 机制层强制，既保证最后一段 prefill 能采出第一个生成 token，也避免状态机死锁；`reusable_blocks`、CPU 查询窗口、`active_prefix_hashes` 全部服从它。
481	- **salt 从链头混入**：`new_request` 的 LoRA 名经 `compute_salt_hash` 折进每个块的哈希，同 token 异身份的请求互相不可见——隔离发生在键空间，GPU 池、offload 查询、事件流一层生效。
482	- `probe_prefix` 产出的 `PrefixProbe` 区分四个口径：`gpu_hit_blocks`（GPU 命中）、`held_blocks`（强引用钉住的）、`reusable_blocks`（min(held, cacheable)）、`cpu_query_window`（还需查 CPU 层的）。
483	- `match_and_add_prefix` 把命中块挂进请求指派表、`kv_position` 前移命中 token 数，且必须在首次 `schedule_prefill` 之前调用；`up_to` 变体允许主动选更短边界。
484	- 回收双路：显式 `evict_inactive` 冷冲刷（qwen3 还用它制造纯 L2 模式），隐性 `allocate` 从 LRU 最旧端弹出；release 的注册块进非活跃池，命中即复活。
485	
486	## 7. 下一步学习建议
487	
488	本讲只讲了 GPU 池内的命中与回收；`PrefixProbe` 的另一半——`cpu_query_hashes` → `reserve_loaded_blocks` → `commit_loaded_blocks` 的 **CPU 层恢复链路**——是下一讲 u3-l1（恢复-提交：reserve_loaded_blocks 与 KV offload 桥）的主题，那里还会解释 `boundary_hash` 的 lineage 语义与 #704 性能回归锚。建议顺带阅读：
489	
490	- [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs#L428-L472) 的前缀匹配一节，对照本讲 4.3。
491	- [docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md#L1-L17)，看引擎层如何把这些原语接到执行器与准确度门禁上。
492	- 若想看「按引用计数而非物理块计数」的共享前缀陷阱（#403），读同文档的 Pitfalls 一节——它是前缀缓存落地时最容易踩的容量核算坑。

# 前缀缓存：块哈希、匹配与 LoRA salt

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出前缀缓存的缓存键是什么：由「位置 + 块内容 + 父块哈希 + salt」构成的 lineage 哈希链，以及为什么共享前缀的请求会得到完全相同的键。
2. 解释两条匹配规则的动机：**只匹配整块**（partial tail block 永远不参与匹配），以及**永远留下最后一个 prompt token 不缓存**（cacheable = ⌊(n−1)/b⌋）。
3. 走通 `probe_prefix` → `PrefixProbe` 的探测链路，理解 `gpu_hit_blocks` / `cpu_query_window` / `held_blocks` / `reusable_blocks` 四个口径的差别。
4. 掌握 `match_and_add_prefix` 如何把已注册块「挂」到新请求上、`kv_position` 如何前移，以及 LoRA 名做 salt 如何实现缓存隔离。
5. 说明回收侧：`evict_inactive`、`active_prefix_hashes` 与上游 `BlockManager` 的 LRU 非活跃池如何配合。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲假设你已读过 u2-l1（BlockPool 与 padding 块）和 u2-l2（RequestKv 生命周期）。在此之上补充四个通俗概念：

- **前缀缓存（prefix cache）**：很多请求共享同一个 prompt 前缀（系统提示词、多轮对话的历史、few-shot 示例）。这些 token 的 K/V 一旦算过一次，后到的请求就没必要再算一遍——把已算好的整块 KV 直接挂给新请求，跳过这部分 prefill。收益非常直观：Qwen3-4B 上一个 ~1900 token 的重复 prompt，首 token 延迟（TTFT）从 141.8ms 降到 16.3ms（约 8.7 倍），见 [docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md:L1-L16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md#L1-L16)。
- **LoRA**：一种轻量微调方案——基座模型权重不动，额外挂一组很小的「适配器」权重参与前向。同一个 prompt 在不同适配器下会算出**不同的 K/V 字节**。这是本讲 salt 机制的直接动因。
- **盐（salt）**：密码学借来的词——计算哈希时混入的一段额外输入。同一个内容配上不同的盐，得到完全不同的哈希。把 LoRA 名当盐混进块哈希链，就能让「同 token 不同适配器」的块永远互相不可见。
- **活跃池 / 非活跃池**：承接 u2-l1 的结论——请求 `release()` 之后，它注册过的完整块不回空闲池，而是进入 LRU 管理的**非活跃池**（可被前缀匹配复活，也可能被回收）；正在被请求持有或被强引用钉住的块在**活跃池**。前缀缓存命中就是从这两个池里「认领」块。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `src/pool.rs` | 本讲主战场：`BlockPool` 的 salt 加链路（`new_request` / `new_request_with_cache_salt`）、探测（`probe_prefix` / `PrefixProbe`）、匹配（`RequestKv::match_and_add_prefix*`）、回收（`evict_inactive` / `active_prefix_hashes`），以及一组纯逻辑内联测试 |
| `tests/lifecycle.rs` | 需 CUDA 的集成测试，含本讲核心例证 `lora_salt_isolates_prefix_cache` |
| `Cargo.toml` | `dynamo-kv-hashing` 依赖（`compute_salt_hash` 的来源），版本经 workspace 统一钉在一个 git rev 上 |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs` | 上游 `SchedulableSequence`：真正的匹配算法、「留最后一个 token」上限的强制点、`kv_position` 前移 |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/sequence/mod.rs` | 上游哈希链：`BlockSequence::new` 接受 salt，`all_sequence_hashes` 产出整条 lineage 链 |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/manager/mod.rs` | 上游 `BlockManager::match_blocks`（线性前缀匹配）与 `evict_inactive` |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs` | LRU 非活跃索引：插入即进 LRU、分配时弹最旧、命中即复活 |
| `pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs` | 消费侧真实调用点：`match_and_add_prefix` 与 `probe_prefix` 怎么被引擎用到 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 块哈希链：前缀缓存的键

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

前缀缓存的第一个问题是：**怎么判断「这个块以前算过」？** 答案是给每个完整块算一个内容身份。但单块内容哈希不够——同一个 16-token 片段出现在序列不同位置时语义不同（RoPE 位置编码不同），也不能直接当缓存键。kvbm 的做法是 **lineage 哈希链**：每个块的哈希覆盖「它自己的内容 + 它在序列中的位置 + 父块的哈希」，概念上：

\[
h_0 = H(\text{salt},\ \text{pos}_0,\ c_0), \qquad
h_i = H(\text{salt},\ \text{pos}_i,\ c_i,\ h_{i-1})
\]

这样第 \(i\) 块的哈希实际上代表了「从序列开头到第 \(i\) 块」的完整历史——两个 prompt 只要前缀相同，前缀上每一块的哈希都逐位相同；一旦某块内容分叉，它和之后所有块的哈希全部不同。源码注释的原话是 "position + content + parent fragment, so block `i` of prompt `P` hashes the same no matter which request computed it"（见 [src/pool.rs:L635-L642](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L635-L642)）。

第二条设计：**salt 从链头就混入**。salt 变了，整条链从 \(h_0\) 起全部改变——这就是 LoRA 隔离的全部原理。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

- 请求创建时：`tokens + block_size + salt` → `TokenBlockSequence`，内部为每个**封满**的块推导 lineage 哈希。
- 查询键：`all_sequence_hashes()` 返回所有完整块的哈希，按序列顺序排列；尾部不满的块不出现在链上（**只匹配整块**规则的哈希侧体现）。
- 跨层寻址：`sequence_hash_bytes` 把 128 位哈希打包成大端 16 字节，供 KV-offload 的 CPU 层当内容键使用。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

上游 `BlockSequence` 的构造接受 salt，并暴露整条哈希链（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/sequence/mod.rs:L220-L251](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/sequence/mod.rs#L220-L251)）：

```rust
pub fn new(tokens: Vec<Token>, block_size: u32, salt_hash: Option<SaltHash>) -> Self {
    let tokens = Tokens::from(tokens);
    Self { sequence: TokenBlockSequence::new(tokens, block_size, salt_hash) }
}
...
/// Returns all sequence hashes from completed blocks.
pub fn all_sequence_hashes(&self) -> Vec<SequenceHash> {
    self.sequence.blocks().iter().map(|b| b.kvbm_sequence_hash()).collect()
}
```

这段代码做了什么：salt 在序列构造时就进入哈希推导；`all_sequence_hashes` 只对 `blocks()`（已封满的块）取哈希——尾部的半块天然被排除。

16 字节内容键的打包在 [src/pool.rs:L735-L739](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L735-L739)：

```rust
fn sequence_hash_bytes(hash: &SequenceHash) -> [u8; 16] {
    hash.as_u128().to_be_bytes()
}
```

这段代码做了什么：把 lineage 哈希转成大端 16 字节，作为 offload 层（CPU/SSD）寻址块的稳定线上格式（该机制的完整恢复链路是 u3-l1 的主题）。

哈希链的两条关键性质由内联测试 `prompt_block_hashes_stable_across_shared_prefix` 守护（[src/pool.rs:L749-L776](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L749-L776)）：两个 64-token 请求共享前 48 个 token，断言前 3 块哈希逐位相等、第 4 块（内容分叉处）必不相等；末尾还断言换一个 LoRA 名后**第 0 块**哈希就不同：

```rust
// A different LoRA salt must poison the match — same tokens, new keys.
let c = pool.new_request(shared, 8, Some("adapter-x"));
assert_ne!(c.prompt_block_hashes()[0], ha[0],
    "salt (lora) must scope the prefix cache");
```

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：亲眼确认「共享前缀哈希一致、分叉即全变、salt 毒化整条链」三条性质。
2. **操作步骤**：先笔头预测——prompt A = 48 个共享 token + 16 个 `7000..` token，prompt B = 同样 48 个共享 token + 16 个 `9000..` token，block_size = 16，各产出几块哈希？哪些相等？然后运行（纯逻辑、无需 GPU）：

### 4.2 PrefixProbe：probe_prefix 与加盐链路

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

探测（probe）回答的问题是：「这个 prompt 的前缀，现在 GPU 上已经有多少块？」它**不创建请求、不预约调度**，只产出一个只读的 `PrefixProbe`。它的原始动机是 KV offload 的 CPU 层预取（u3-l1 详讲），但它的字段清晰地划分了四个容易混淆的「块数」口径：

- `gpu_hit_blocks`：GPU 上已经命中的连续前缀块数。
- `held_blocks`：探针实际用强引用**钉住**的块数（GPU 命中 + 之后从 CPU 层提交进来的块）。
- `reusable_blocks`：真正允许被请求复用的块数 = `min(held, cacheable)`。
- `cpu_query_window`：还需要去 CPU 层查询的块数 = `cacheable − gpu_hit`。

其中「可复用上限」服从本讲最重要的公式。设 prompt 长度为 \(n\)、块大小为 \(b\)：

\[
\text{cacheable} = \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{b} \right\rfloor
\]

即**永远比「整条 prompt 能凑出的满块数」少留出至少一个 token**。若 \(n\) 恰为 \(b\) 的整数倍，则最后**一整块**都不可复用。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
probe_prefix(prompt, lora)
  └─ probe_prefix_with_cache_salt(prompt, cache_salt=None, lora)
       ├─ new_request_with_cache_salt(prompt, 0, cache_salt, lora)
       │     ├─ salt_hash = compute_salt_hash(cache_salt, lora)   ← 加盐点
       │     └─ SchedulableSequence::new(..., Some(salt_hash))    ← 链头混入
       ├─ seq_hashes = 该临时请求的 all_sequence_hashes()
       ├─ cacheable = (n - 1) / block_size                        ← 留最后一个 token
       └─ gpu_guard = block_manager.match_blocks(&seq_hashes)     ← 线性前缀匹配
  → PrefixProbe { seq_hashes, gpu_hit, cacheable, block_size, held: gpu_guard }
```

注意：公共入口 `probe_prefix` 固定 `cache_salt = None`，`cache_salt` 变体目前是 crate 私有（`fn` 而非 `pub fn`），供 MTP 等「同样 token 会因块外状态产生不同 KV」的场景在 crate 内部使用——对外公开的身份维度只有 `lora_name`。

### 4.3 match_and_add_prefix：挂前缀与「永远留最后一个 token」

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

匹配是前缀缓存的**消费**动作：在请求第一次 `schedule_prefill` 之前调用一次，把命中的整块直接挂进该请求的块指派表，返回可跳过的 token 数，`kv_position` 同步前移——之后 prefill 只需转发剩余后缀。「永远留最后一个 token」在 kvbm 上游被强制执行，理由有二（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs:L428-L441](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs#L428-L441) 的注释原文）：

1. **采样需要**：最后一段 prefill 必须跑，才能用最后一个位置的 logits 采样出**第一个生成 token**（全命中会导致无 forward 可做）。
2. **状态机合法性**：全命中会让调度状态机「prefill 完成、悬空 token 数为 0」——没有合法的下一步，直接死锁。

qwen3 的实践文档还注明 vLLM 采用同样的规则（[docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md:L9-L16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md#L9-L16)）。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
fresh RequestKv（尚未 schedule_prefill）
  └─ match_and_add_prefix(pool)            ← 公共入口
       └─ match_and_add_prefix_up_to(pool, usize::MAX)
            └─ kvbm SchedulableSequence::match_and_add_prefix_up_to(manager, max)
                 ├─ max_blocks = min(⌊(n−1)/b⌋, requested_max)   ← 双重上限
                 ├─ 沿哈希链匹配、把命中块挂进 assignments
                 └─ prefill_position += count·b;  kv_position = prefill_position
  返回 count × block_size（token 数）
之后：schedule_prefill 只需覆盖剩余后缀；chunk_start 直接取 kv_position
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

本 crate 的薄包装（[src/pool.rs:L393-L423](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L393-L423)）：

```rust

/// their prefill. Returns the number of cached tokens; `kv_position()`
/// advances by the same amount. Must be called on a fresh request,
/// before the first `schedule_prefill`.
///
/// Matching always leaves at least one prompt token uncached so the
/// final prefill chunk can emit the first generated token.
pub fn match_and_add_prefix(&mut self, pool: &BlockPool) -> anyhow::Result<usize> {
    self.match_and_add_prefix_up_to(pool, usize::MAX)
}
```

`match_and_add_prefix_up_to` 的包装体还做一件事：把事件光标 `emitted_blocks` 直接设到当前已指派块数——前缀命中的块**不再**向 KV 路由发 store 事件，因为最先封存它们的请求已经发过（[src/pool.rs:L409-L423](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L409-L423)，事件流本身是 u3-l2 的主题）。返回值以 token 计：`blocks * self.seq.block_size()`。

```rust

    .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("prefix match should not produce duplicates"));

    self.kv_position = self.prefill_position;

```

这段代码做了什么：即使调用方传 `usize::MAX`，kvbm 仍按 ⌊(n−1)/b⌋ 截断——**final-token 规则在机制层强制，不依赖调用方自觉**；匹配后 `kv_position` 与 `prefill_position` 一起跳到命中块覆盖的末尾。

`up_to` 变体的存在理由（同文件注释）：混合注意力模型的辅助状态可能只能在**短于最长 KV 命中**的边界上恢复，所以允许调用方主动选一个更短的精确边界。配套查询 `prefix_matched_blocks`（[src/pool.rs:L683-L686](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L683-L686)）与 `registered_boundary_hash`（[src/pool.rs:L425-L446](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L425-L446)）让调用方核对「实际挂上了几块、边界哈希是否与探测器一致」。

```rust
req.cached_tokens = Some(matched);
```

这段代码做了什么：qwen3 executor 在请求的第一个 prefill 分块前匹配，把跳过量记到 `cached_tokens`，后续分块起点直接取 `kv_position`。注释还说明 prompt logprobs 请求会**跳过匹配**——打分需要每个位置的 logits，缓存位置不转发。

### 4.4 回收：evict_inactive、active_prefix_hashes 与 LRU 后端

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

缓存必须有回收，否则非活跃池无限膨胀。本 crate 的回收面有三个部件：

- `BlockPool::evict_inactive`：**一次性清空**非活跃池（冷缓存冲刷）。使用中的块（活跃池）不受影响。它也是 offload 路径上「把前缀赶出 HBM、逼下一个请求从 CPU 层恢复」的手段。
- `BlockPool::active_prefix_hashes`：只查**活跃池**前缀，不晋升非活跃条目、不钉住块——一个「看一眼还活着多长前缀」的只读探照灯。
- 上游 LRU 非活跃索引：块释放 → 进 LRU；新分配缺块 → 从 LRU 最旧端弹出复用；前缀命中 → 从索引中弹出（复活为活跃）。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
请求 release()
  └─ 注册过的完整块 → 非活跃池（LRU 索引: SequenceHash → BlockId）
       ├─ 后续请求 match_blocks 命中 → 从 LRU 弹出，挂为新请求的活跃块（复活）
       ├─ allocate_blocks 需要块 → pop_lru，最旧条目回空闲池（隐性回收）
       └─ evict_inactive() → 全部倒回空闲池（显式冲刷）
```

LRU 的排序口径值得注意：模块自述为 "least-recently-**inserted** block evicted first"（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs:L1-L27](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs#L1-L27)）——因为命中即弹出（复活），留在索引里的条目从未被再次触及，插入序就是有效的年龄序。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

本 crate 的两个回收面入口（[src/pool.rs:L125-L146](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L125-L146)）：

```rust
/// Evict every cached-but-unused block from the GPU prefix cache (drain the
/// inactive pool). In-use blocks are untouched. A cold-cache flush — and,
/// for the offload path, the way to force a prefix out of HBM so a
/// subsequent request must restore it from the CPU tier.
pub fn evict_inactive(&self) {
    self.block_manager.evict_inactive();
}

/// Return active prompt-prefix hashes without promoting inactive entries or
/// keeping the matched blocks alive.
pub fn active_prefix_hashes(&self, prompt_tokens: Vec<u32>, lora_name: Option<&str>)
    -> Vec<[u8; 16]>
{
    let num_input = prompt_tokens.len();
    let request = self.new_request(prompt_tokens, 0, lora_name);
    let hashes = request.seq.inner().sequence().all_sequence_hashes();
    let cacheable = num_input.saturating_sub(1) / self.block_size;
    let active = self.block_manager.active_prefix_len(&hashes).min(cacheable);
    ...
}
```

这段代码做了什么：`evict_inactive` 是显式冲刷；`active_prefix_hashes` 复用同一条加盐哈希链，但走 `active_prefix_len`——只统计仍被强引用持有的连续前缀长度，且同样被 cacheable 封顶（salt 维度一致，跨身份查询自然 miss）。

上游的两副面孔（[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/manager/mod.rs:L87-L95](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/manager/mod.rs#L87-L95) 与 [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs:L65-L86](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/pools/inactive/backends/lru_backend.rs#L65-L86)）：

```rust
// manager: drain 非活跃池，活跃块（含 padding 预留）不受影响
pub fn evict_inactive(&self) {
    drop(self.store.drain_inactive_to_mutable());
}

// LRU 后端: 分配缺块时从最旧端弹出（隐性回收）
fn allocate(&mut self, count: usize) -> Vec<(SequenceHash, BlockId)> {
    for _ in 0..count {
        if let Some(entry) = self.cache.pop_lru() { allocated.push(entry); } ...
}

fn insert(&mut self, seq_hash: SequenceHash, block_id: BlockId) {
    assert!(self.cache.len() < self.cache.cap().get(),
        "LRU backend insert would cause eviction! ...");
```

这段代码做了什么：回收有两条路——**显式** `evict_inactive` 全量冲刷、**隐性** `allocate` 从 LRU 最旧端取；`insert` 的断言表明 LRU 容量按「能装下全部块」配置，正常路径绝不静默丢条目。

消费侧的一个真实用法（[pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L2505-L2521](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L2505-L2521)）：纯 L2 模式下，qwen3 在探测前先 `evict_inactive()` 清掉跨请求的 HBM 留存，让 `probe_prefix` 看到 `gpu_hit == 0`、整段可复用前缀都去 CPU 层查询——evict 在这里是「测量开关」而不是内存压力应对。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：验证「release 之后前缀进非活跃池：`active_prefix_hashes` 变空，但匹配仍可命中」的活跃/非活跃分野。
2. **操作步骤**：阅读并运行内联测试 `active_prefix_hashes_exclude_reclaimable_entries`（[src/pool.rs:L778-L789](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L778-L789)，纯逻辑无 GPU）：

   ```bash
   cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --lib active_prefix_hashes -- --nocapture
   ```

   场景：40-token prompt，prefill 32 token（2 块）后——`active_prefix_hashes` 长度为 2（块仍被请求持有）；`release()` 之后——立刻变空。
3. **需要观察的现象**：两段断言先后通过：持有期 2、释放后 0。
4. **预期结果**：如上。随后思考：此时若 `match_and_add_prefix` 同 prompt 新请求，仍能命中 2 块（块在**非活跃池**里，`match_blocks` 同时查两个池）——这正是 4.3 实践里 `lora_salt_isolates_prefix_cache` 的前半段铺垫。待本地验证。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`evict_inactive` 会不会误伤正在服务的请求？padding 块会不会被清掉？
**答案**：都不会。它只 drain 非活跃池；在用块由请求的强引用保持在活跃池。padding 块被 `std::mem::forget` 的 RAII 把手钉死在活跃池（u2-l1），天然免疫。

**练习 2**：非活跃池里的块什么时候被**隐性**回收？
**答案**：新请求分配块而空闲池不足时，`allocate` 从 LRU 最旧端弹出条目归还复用——最老的缓存前缀最先牺牲，无需任何显式调用。

**练习 3**：`active_prefix_hashes` 与 `probe_prefix` 都走同一条哈希链，差别在哪？
**答案**：`probe_prefix` 经 `match_blocks` 拿强引用、会复活非活跃命中、还给 offload 提供查询窗口；`active_prefix_hashes` 走 `active_prefix_len`，只统计活跃前缀、不晋升不钉住，适合「只看不动」的观测场景。

## 5. 综合实践

把本讲三个机制（加盐哈希链、匹配挂前缀、非活跃池复活）串成一个完整剧本——这就是规格指定的核心实践：**复现 `lora_salt_isolates_prefix_cache` 的场景并补全状态追踪**。

**任务设定**：`KvCacheManager` 以 32 块、block_size=16 建池（1 块 padding → 31 可用）。prompt 为 48 个 `7`（3 个满块）。

**步骤**（参照 [tests/lifecycle.rs:L237-L270](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/tests/lifecycle.rs#L237-L270) 逐行跟踪，先填表再跑测试）：

| 步骤 | 操作 | 预期 `available_blocks()` | 预期匹配结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 请求 a（`Some("a")`）`schedule_prefill(48)` + `apply_prefill(42)` | 31 → 28（3 块被占） | — |
| 2 | `a.release()` | 28 → 31（3 块进**非活跃池**，不回空闲池也计为可用） | — |
| 3 | 基座请求（`None`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31 | **0**：salt 不同，哈希链从第 0 块就不同 |
| 4 | 请求 b（`Some("b")`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31 | **0**：同上 |
| 5 | 请求 a2（`Some("a")`）`match_and_add_prefix` | 31（2 块从非活跃池复活为活跃） | **32**：3 块全部哈希命中，但 cacheable = ⌊47/16⌋ = 2 钳掉 1 块 |

验证命令（需 CUDA）：

```bash
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --test lifecycle lora_salt -- --nocapture
```

无 GPU 时用等价的纯逻辑内联测试覆盖同一机制（cache_salt 维度）：`cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --lib cache_salt_isolates -- --nocapture`（[src/pool.rs:L791-L835](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L791-L835)，其中还能看到探测路径同样被隔离：错误 salt 的 `probe_prefix` 得 `gpu_hit_blocks() == 0`）。断言数值待本地验证。

**最后回答规格的问题：如果去掉 salt，两个不同 LoRA 适配器会出什么正确性事故？**

块哈希将只由 token 内容、位置与父链决定——适配器 a 注册的块与适配器 b 的请求算出**完全相同的键**。于是 b 的 `match_and_add_prefix` 会命中 a 算出的块，跳过这段 prefill，注意力内核随后拿着**用 a 的权重算出的 K/V** 去和 **b 的权重算出的 Q** 做点积。这不是崩溃，而是**静默的输出污染**：分布悄悄漂移，没有任何断言或错误会触发（源码注释的措辞正是 "K/V computed with different weights can't be **silently** reused"——salt 的作用就是让这种复用在键空间里直接不可能，而不是在挂载时检查）。反向同样成立：基座请求会误吃 LoRA 块、LoRA 请求会误吃基座块。由于同一条哈希链还被 offload 的 CPU 层查询与路由事件复用，隔离在键推导处做一次，所有层自动生效。

## 6. 本讲小结

- 前缀缓存的键是 **lineage 哈希链**：位置 + 块内容 + 父块哈希 + salt，共享前缀逐位相同、分叉即全变；尾部半块永不参与（只匹配整块）。
- **永远留最后一个 token**：cacheable = ⌊(n−1)/b⌋ 在 kvbm 机制层强制，既保证最后一段 prefill 能采出第一个生成 token，也避免状态机死锁；`reusable_blocks`、CPU 查询窗口、`active_prefix_hashes` 全部服从它。
- **salt 从链头混入**：`new_request` 的 LoRA 名经 `compute_salt_hash` 折进每个块的哈希，同 token 异身份的请求互相不可见——隔离发生在键空间，GPU 池、offload 查询、事件流一层生效。
- `probe_prefix` 产出的 `PrefixProbe` 区分四个口径：`gpu_hit_blocks`（GPU 命中）、`held_blocks`（强引用钉住的）、`reusable_blocks`（min(held, cacheable)）、`cpu_query_window`（还需查 CPU 层的）。
- `match_and_add_prefix` 把命中块挂进请求指派表、`kv_position` 前移命中 token 数，且必须在首次 `schedule_prefill` 之前调用；`up_to` 变体允许主动选更短边界。
- 回收双路：显式 `evict_inactive` 冷冲刷（qwen3 还用它制造纯 L2 模式），隐性 `allocate` 从 LRU 最旧端弹出；release 的注册块进非活跃池，命中即复活。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲只讲了 GPU 池内的命中与回收；`PrefixProbe` 的另一半——`cpu_query_hashes` → `reserve_loaded_blocks` → `commit_loaded_blocks` 的 **CPU 层恢复链路**——是下一讲 u3-l1（恢复-提交：reserve_loaded_blocks 与 KV offload 桥）的主题，那里还会解释 `boundary_hash` 的 lineage 语义与 #704 性能回归锚。建议顺带阅读：

- [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/integrations/scheduled.rs#L428-L472) 的前缀匹配一节，对照本讲 4.3。
- [docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/docs/models/qwen3/prefix-cache.md#L1-L17)，看引擎层如何把这些原语接到执行器与准确度门禁上。
- 若想看「按引用计数而非物理块计数」的共享前缀陷阱（#403），读同文档的 Pitfalls 一节——它是前缀缓存落地时最容易踩的容量核算坑。

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool.
